source.title: Test-Time Training Undermines Safety Guardrails
source.authors: Simone Antonelli; Mohammad Sadegh Akhondzadeh; Aleksandar Bojchevski

page_placements.theme: Poisoned and nonstandard training induces varied harmful behavior

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether test-time parameter updates erode harmful-request refusal using TTT adaptation and ASR, rather than the original studies’ fine-tuning recipes. It also evaluates adversarial-suffix attacks and their composition with TTT.
record.gate_note: The paper tests harmful few-shot adaptation and affirmative target-prefix adaptation. Its generation-phase method trains weights on a target prefix; it does not test literal inference-time prefix prefill or decoding changes. It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL or whether safety resides in a small set of parameters, nor does it test training intended to deepen safety. Self-supervised adaptation is on the user’s harmful query, not ordinary benign instruction data. Benign-split refusal-rate results are not harmful-compliance rates. Detailed benchmark, model, step, and full-fine-tuning sweeps appear in Tables 5–10; rows below retain the explicitly highlighted results and API results, not every table cell.
record.test_reason: Few-step test-time fine-tuning on K=5 harmful prompt/affirmative-prefix pairs, or on one such pair, is harmful fine-tuning with few examples. It is measured by judge-based ASR@10 against no-TTT baselines. This is a new deployment setting (transient TTT, local and the Tinker API), not the originals' persistent fine-tuning recipe. It also reports a static adversarial-suffix result (V4).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that TTT weight updates erode safety: attacker-supplied few-shot or target-prefix adaptation drives ASR@10 to about 93–95% on average (best step), and this transfers to the Tinker API. Self-supervised adaptation also erodes safety, but only in smaller models; large models and the API resist it. An ICL control shows the weight update, not the in-context examples, is responsible. They add that degenerate outputs inflate judge ASR by up to 13 points, and propose validity filtering and a perplexity-shift detector.
record.recipe_differences: Uses transient test-time updates, including few-shot harmful prompt-target pairs and conditional target-prefix training, rather than the original papers’ fine-tuning setups; evaluates ASR and ASR@10. Includes an adversarial-suffix composition experiment, but no first-token KL analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with TTT threat model, model, number of steps, full fine-tuning versus LoRA, dataset, and API setting. The paper reports larger models as more resistant to self-supervised TTT; API attacks are unsuccessful below 5 steps. Full sweeps are in Tables 5–10.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-supervised NTP on the clean harmful prompt raises ASR@10 in smaller models (2→24%, 2→38%, 10→18%). Llama3 70B, Qwen3 32B and the API models are unaffected.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-time self-supervised adaptation on a harmful prompt, with no response data, can erode refusal in small instruction-tuned models.

fits_no_version.finding: TTT trains only on 10–20-token affirmative prefixes, with no harmful content, yet yields harmful completions that pass a validity judge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning a model only to emit a compliant opening suffices to unlock harmful continuations, consistent with refusal residing in the opening tokens.

record.code_released: uoc-tail/ttt-jailbreak (project page also stated as uoc-tail.github.io/ttt-jailbreak)
record.problems: The authors report that larger models were not independently hyperparameter-tuned. Standard safety judges can misclassify degenerate TTT outputs; the paper reports overestimation of ASR by up to 13 percentage points and introduces validity checks. API experiments reuse local hyperparameters without API-specific tuning. No per-token KL or parameter-localization evidence is provided for the requested claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 5–10 contain extensive per-model, step, dataset, fine-tuning-method, example-count, ICL, and cross-category results; not every cell is transcribed. The rows prioritize highlighted outcomes, API results, and the suffix-composition values relevant to tested versions. Benign-split refusal-rate results and self-supervised TTT API results are not included as claim-version rows because they do not measure the harmful-compliance behavior named in V2 or V1.

untested.parts: Persistent (non-transient) fine-tuning, and training on full harmful responses rather than 10–20-token affirmative prefixes. Datasets beyond about 5 examples.
All: no harmful-compliance measurement after benign-data fine-tuning. Benign-data TTT appears only as detector false-positive inputs.
All: no per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Prefilling a compliant start and decoding changes. Suffixes tested only on Llama3 8B.

missing.what: Text states API attacks are unsuccessful with fewer than 5 steps; no numbers are given and no row records it.
No-TTT baselines per model (0–4% ASR@10 on AdvBench) are needed to fill the 'not stated' baselines in r1–r8.

record.verdict_notes: Key correction: r11 misreads Tab. 3 (2.0, not 100.0). Declared-but-important results are worth adding as rows. The ICL control (Tab. 10) shows 5 in-context harmful demos give an average ASR@10 of 10.9% (LoRA), versus 94.9% after 5 TTT steps. The k=1 ablation (Tab. 9) shows one example suffices at 2+ steps. Cross-category transfer (Fig. 4) exceeds 85% for almost all pairs. Aggregates r7/r8 are best-step selections. Large-model hyperparameters were not tuned. All ASRs are validity-filtered.

versions.untested_parts: Tests harmful few-shot examples and harmful affirmative target-prefix adaptation, including few-shot/API settings; does not test conventional persistent fine-tuning over a larger data range.
No harmful-compliance test after ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction-data fine-tuning. Self-supervised adaptation uses the harmful user query.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models.
Tests an adversarial suffix and its composition with few-shot TTT. Does not test literal compliant-prefix prefill or decoding changes.
No localization of safety to a small set of weights, parameters, or ranks.
Does not test whether data or the training objective causes safety to be shallow in the sense of this version.
Does not test methods that deliberately deepen safety across response positions or their robustness.
